problems.title: Keep explicit corrections during confidence filtering
problems.need: Corrected points and unscored predictions can both have NaN confidence; existing filtering cannot distinguish them. Existing edit provenance can supply that distinction.
problems.proposal: Optional explicit edited mask for movement confidence filtering.
problems.baseline: movement already stores edited flags; PR #1037 provides a coarse NaN policy.
problems.integration: Existing movement function in scripts/notebooks after napari native save/reload.
problems.unknown: Covers only a filtering subproblem of #1027; no acceptance or researcher benefit established.
problems.next: Reconcile API choice with the original request; preserve coordinate semantics and distinguish technical verification from adoption.
problems.audience: Researchers cleaning pose tracks after manually correcting body-part positions in napari.
problems.value: Keep deliberate corrections while removing other predictions with missing confidence; fewer lost corrections is a hypothesis until assessed in real use.

page.title: Keep manual pose corrections during filtering
page.summary: A person corrects a tracked body-part position, saves the dataset, then filters low-confidence predictions. The corrected point can be removed because its confidence is missing—the same condition used for other unscored predictions.
page.solution: The patch lets the existing confidence filter accept explicit edited flags. With missing-score retention disabled, it can keep a deliberately corrected point while dropping an unedited prediction with a missing score. Omitting the new input preserves the existing policy.
page.science: Pose estimates are coordinates, while confidence scores describe the model output. A manual-edit flag describes where a correction came from. It does not prove the corrected coordinates are scientifically accurate.
terms: Keypoint
A named body-part position at a particular time.
NaN
A missing numeric value. Here, a missing confidence score does not tell us whether a person corrected the point.
Edit provenance
A record that a value was deliberately edited, separate from its numeric position and confidence.

Open a constructed movement dataset in the real host.
Correct a position

Save and reload
The host writes and reloads the edited dataset.

page.comparisonNote: This comparison disables retention of missing confidence scores in both cases. The existing default can instead keep all missing-score points; it cannot make the explicit-edit distinction.

problems.title: Inspect pairwise IoU / OKS while tuning duplicate filtering
problems.need: Choosing overlap method and threshold requires guessing pairwise scores.
problems.proposal: Read-only pose inspector showing both OKS directions, threshold boundaries and full-frame decisions.
problems.baseline: SLEAP has QC, editing and filter settings; pinned audit found no pairwise comparison panel.
problems.integration: Local demo now; future read-only SLEAP selection adapter or explicit pose import.
problems.unknown: Frozen synthetic examples only; not in SLEAP, no arbitrary file input, no measured benefit. Discussion #2815 and issue #2816 are one source family.

page.title: Inspect why overlapping poses are removed
page.summary: Two pose predictions can overlap even when they describe different animals or different body-part arrangements. The researcher needs to understand why a duplicate filter keeps one and removes another.
page.solution: The browser prototype adds an overlay, pair measurements, threshold boundaries and score-order context around an unchanged filter. A separate experimental SLEAP 1.6.6 source adapter now inspects actual host instances read-only, with both directional OKS values and stored confidence fields. The project record links its installation and recorded host walkthrough. Neither capability improves the prediction model.
page.science: A pose is an estimated set of body-part positions. Tracking software can produce multiple candidate poses in one video frame. A duplicate filter compares candidates and can remove a later candidate when their similarity exceeds a chosen threshold.
terms: IoU
Intersection over union: how much two bounding boxes overlap relative to their combined area.
OKS
Object keypoint similarity: a score based on corresponding body-part positions and scale. This implementation’s score can depend on comparison direction.
Suppression
Removing a candidate pose from the filter output; this is not evidence that it was biologically wrong.

Apply the threshold

Inspect the decision
The prototype exposes the selected pair and full-frame context.
page.comparisonNote: Both views use the same fixed input and filter. For the swapped-label example at IoU threshold 0.8, A is retained and B is suppressed in both views. The added capability is explanation.

page.title: Keep streamed neural data intact during inspection
page.summary: A converter checks a stream of samples before writing an NWB file. The inspection can consume part of the stream, leaving the later writer with missing values that become zeros in the saved file.
page.solution: The patch reuses HDMF’s existing shape helper instead of the Inspector’s local helper. In the tested wrapped-stream workflow, inspection no longer consumes data that the writer still needs. An upstream proposal already suggested helper reuse; Kufu’s contribution is the bounded patch, reproduction and regression evidence.
page.science: Neurophysiology recordings can be large, so software may handle them a chunk at a time. The saved sample sequence must match the input. Preserving samples is a data-integrity requirement; it does not establish that the experiment or its interpretation is correct.
terms: NWB
Neurodata Without Borders: a format and ecosystem for organising neurophysiology data.
Stream / iterator
A source that yields successive chunks; reading a single-pass source advances it.
Shape inspection
Asking how many samples and channels an object contains, without intentionally analysing the signal.
workflow: Receive a stream
Constructed positive samples arrive in chunks.
Inspect before writing
The real Inspector checks the NWB object.
Save and reopen
The real HDF5 or Zarr writer and reader execute.
Compare every value
The replay checks the complete sequence and dtype against input.
page.comparisonTitle: Before and after the inspection patch
page.comparisonNote: The input contains no zeros. The baseline returns inspection errors, but writing still succeeds; it must not be described as a silently passing inspection. Uninspected controls preserve the data.

page.title: Preserve a supplied age of zero
page.summary: A dataset supplies an age value of zero. During metadata processing, software treats zero as false and leaves the exported age empty. A known value has become indistinguishable from a missing annotation.
page.solution: The patch preserves zero in refine.bio’s harmoniser and model metadata output while retaining existing handling of empty or unknown values. The tested path creates real sample records and writes actual TSV/JSON metadata files. It does not infer missing ages or change their units.
page.science: Sample metadata describes the biological material being analysed. Researchers use those annotations when selecting or comparing samples. A numeric zero and an absent value have different meanings; this software check preserves what was supplied without interpreting the biology.
terms: Harmonisation
Turning supplied annotations into consistent fields and representations.
Truthiness check
A programming condition that treats numeric zero as false, alongside values such as an empty string.
TSV / JSON
Text file formats used here for actual metadata exports.

demonstrations.title: Pairwise overlap inspector
demonstrations.runtime: Browser: offline, no model or Python runtime needed.
demonstrations.inputs: Seven fixed, clearly labelled synthetic pose examples with missing/degenerate nodes and two/three-instance contexts.
demonstrations.expected: Changing metric, threshold or score order shows the retained/suppressed/unavailable instances for the pinned filter.
demonstrations.verification: 498 actual CPU FilterPipeline calls; browser checks cover all 168 decision boundaries. Build and browser results are separate evidence.
demonstrations.limits: Frozen inputs; no SLEAP selection integration, arbitrary file input or proven researcher benefit.

demonstrations.title: movement edit-aware filtering replay
demonstrations.runtime: Python 3.13, pinned movement checkout plus approved patch; real Qt widgets in offscreen mode.
demonstrations.inputs: Constructed pose Dataset only; moved, removed, missing and unscored points across individuals.
demonstrations.expected: Explicit filtering keeps the correction and drops the unscored prediction; removed positions stay missing. Repeated export still loses deletion flags.

demonstrations.title: NWB stream preservation replay
demonstrations.runtime: Complete CPython 3.13.9 in a short-lived Vercel Sandbox for requested experiments; the pinned local/CI replay remains available.
demonstrations.inputs: Synthetic int16 signals with configurable rows, channels, buffer, seed, pattern, HDF5/Zarr format and iterator type. The recorded CI matrix uses two channels and 50, 100 or 500 rows; no recordings.
demonstrations.expected: Baseline inspection loses 50, 100 or 300 rows; the patch preserves all values across both backends and iterator types.
demonstrations.verification: 12 inspected cases and 12 uninspected controls per revision; 341 broader unit tests passed and 5 skipped. The replay passed in the required scientific check in main run 40613968067; fresh results reached the verified protected production release. The protected Vercel preview also passed real queued HDF5/Zarr runs, private download verification, stopped compute and retained timestamped progress.
demonstrations.limits: Bounded synthetic inputs only; no uploaded recordings, arbitrary code, full version matrix, real-recording evaluation or upstream acceptance.
demonstrations.command:
# Follow the pinned environment and patch setup in the project record.
python projects/nwb-stream-integrity/verify.py --expect patched --output /tmp/nwb-patched.json

demonstrations.title: Zero-age metadata workflow replay
demonstrations.runtime: Maintained Linux CI replay using the pinned upstream R 3.4.4 base and PostgreSQL 14.24; local ingestion/migration replay also passed on PostgreSQL 16.2.
demonstrations.inputs: Five constructed SRA metadata cases through the actual worker path, plus 28 harmoniser cases; no research files or live API calls.
demonstrations.expected: Both zero-age cases change from empty to 0.000 in actual TSV files; positive age remains 2.000 and empty/unknown stay empty in all three aggregation modes.
demonstrations.verification: Actual TSV/JSON export and five existing metadata regressions per revision passed in CI run 40763058912, with 91 migrations, real startup registration, retained TSV text and independently checked file hashes.
demonstrations.limits: Constructed workflow and pinned runtime only. No expression processing, scheduler/upload, populated-production upgrade, full upstream suite or measured researcher benefit.
